title: Research notes (no κ claim): #109 and lower bounds, the coding gap, a Lorentzian minrank obstruction, and a loss chain
body:
**No κ claim.** This PR adds only `research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/`, which contains four notes, their scripts and
DRUP proofs. No supplier, certificate or existing file changes. Based on `main` at `17ce0c7`.

## Summary

| # | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #109 contradicts no unconditional lower bound for multiplication. Each bound fails on a stated hypothesis (on-line, bounded coefficients, well-conditioning, or Li–Li). | audit |
| 1 | **Lemma B′:** #109's machine can be made oblivious at the same κ: fixed-width scalars, compute-both branches, and an oblivious Schönhage–Strassen whose log log factor fits the p^κ margin that `08-assembly.tex` already reserves. So **if #109's Theorem 1 holds, multiplication has bounded-degree Boolean circuits of size O(n(log n)^{1−κ})**. | proved, given a procedure-by-procedure audit (included) |
| 1 | **If #109 holds, on-line multitape multiplication is slower than off-line by Ω((log n)^κ)** (Paterson–Fischer–Meyer). So no relaxed variant of #109's transforms can have (log n)^{o(1)} overhead. | proved, given #109 |
| 2 | **The rank saving is a coding gap.** On #109's labelled exchange network, weighted by rank or subspace distance, coding achieves rate 1 while flow ≤ (s + 2W)/(Wm + 2W). This is < 1 exactly when s < Wm. It reproduces the paper's η exactly, and it is the same mechanism as dysfunctor's 33-vertex Li–Li counterexample, whose flow we re-certify as exactly 149/150. | proved (analytic LP dual) + exact |
| 3 | **I_{11,1} and I_{13,1} (triples + pairs) have fitting minrank n, not n − 1**, over every field of characteristic ≠ 2. E8 = I_{9,1} is the case n − 9 = 0. | proved; SAT step exhaustive with drat-trim-checked DRUP proofs; exact ranks over Q |
| 4 | **Loss chain**: a ≈ (1/m)(D/W)/L_ent, with L_ent = ln m − E ln r. It reproduces gen4, #493, #501, #589 and the selected #596 supplier to < 10⁻⁸; the #596 row gives main's κ. There is also a piece-count remark: under H1–H6 no label family reaches κ → 1 (copy-free windows give a ≲ 0.31/(h − 1)). | exact; Theorems 1 and 4 proved; H6 assumed |

## What is new compared with prior work

- **Li–Li is already refuted** (2026-10-07), by Zhang–B. Li–Z. Li (arXiv 2610.09367, already cited in
  `docs/research/stronger-rank-screens.md`), by Braverman–He (arXiv 2610.10108), and by
  [dysfunctor/network-coding-counterexample](https://github.com/dysfunctor/network-coding-counterexample), which
  builds its network from #109's XOR swap. So "#109 ⇒ ¬Li–Li" (via AFKL) is moot and gives no error signal in either
  direction. Note 1 says this explicitly. **What is new is Lemma B′, the circuit corollary and the on-line/off-line
  separation.** We found neither in the preprint, the hub (PRs and comments through #633), openai/math, AFKL,
  HvdH 2021/2025 or the public discussion.
- Note 2 generalises dysfunctor's observation from the XOR swap to the rank-weighted motif with any η > 0, as an
  identity. The 33-vertex flow value is an independent re-check, not a new result.
- Note 1's Ailon row cites #621 and #628 (chafreaky): their length-independent but exponential-in-r conditioning
  bounds for the prime-power cyclic inverses are consistent with the row.
- Note 3 covers a family that #446, #595 (C.6), #598 and #606 (DominikScholz), #620 (GamingPuzzled; ADE and number-field label screens, with #630's E6 → D6 correction by vectorsss), hipotures' lattice screen and
  Sussman's notes do not cover. Unlike #595 C.6, its SAT step ships proof logs.
- Note 4 is complementary to #595 (DreamingOfClouds) and #602 (artuskg). #595's κ ≤ 5.1595·10⁻³ is much tighter
  inside its scope, and its §A.5/§C.7/§E already price helpers, descents and the log-gap. The note claims only the
  four-factor identity and a hypothesis-light piece-count bound. It also lists the route-specific ceilings it sits
  beside: #183, #458, #203, #201 and Swapnil Jain's P1/P2.
- **Dropped as duplicate:** our "a saving needs different scalar and label characteristics" lemma (Swapnil Jain's
  closed ideas; Sussman's mod-2 argument), our frozen-word and E8-architecture ceilings (superseded by #595), and
  our fixed-word retiming optimality results (#556, #557).

## Scope

- Notes 1–2 concern consequences of #109's Theorem 1 *if it holds*. They neither support nor refute it.
- Note 3 is a minrank statement about two graphs. It bounds no supplier, and the general odd-n claim is a conjecture.
- Note 4's remark assumes H1–H6. H6 is checked on the certified words but not proved in general, and the remark is
  not a universal ceiling.
- "Proved" means a written argument checked only by its authors. Nothing here is formalised in Lean, and certificate
  success is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/requirements.txt
DYSFUNCTOR=/path/to/network-coding-counterexample DRAT_TRIM=/path/to/drat-trim \
  bash research/lower-bounds-coding-gap/verify.sh /fresh/out
```

The run took about 75 s from a fresh venv (Python 3.14.4, WSL Ubuntu) on the rebased branch, and every step printed PASS:

- manifest;
- η exact;
- flow 149/150 exact;
- 10,395 cliques;
- final span 7/10/12;
- σ-model 0/130 violations;
- N = 6, 8, 10, 12 UNSAT with drat-trim `s VERIFIED` (fresh and shipped proofs);
- loss chain roots;
- piece-count certificates.

Without `DYSFUNCTOR` the flow check prints SKIP. Without `DRAT_TRIM` the proofs are written and the CNFs compared
byte-for-byte, but the proofs are not checked.
